plain: The idea is that human consciousness began when our primate ancestors found and ate mind-altering mushrooms. It comes from the writer Terence McKenna, and people call it the stoned ape theory. A researcher named Jeffrey Mishlove, who holds a doctorate, sums it up this way: consciousness itself developed when our ancestors discovered these mushrooms. Michels describes McKenna's version himself. A couple of million years ago in Africa, he says, hunter-gatherer bands had to follow animal dung to find their prey. In another episode he says the theory could explain why skull size doubled between Homo habilis, an early human species, and modern humans. The writer Graham Hancock names McKenna's book Food of the Gods as one of the first books to set it out. If it were true, a plant would have helped make us human.
